description: Opening conversation that starts the case and points the player to the photo and the email.

nodes.speaker: lucy
nodes.text: You finally woke up. Good. Blondie is gone, and I don’t think this city plans on giving her back.

options.text: Gone how? Missing, hiding, or dead and nobody told me yet?
You look like you already know more than you’re saying.
What do I have to start with?
You could’ve called someone cheaper.
Did Blondie leave anything else?

nodes.speaker: lucy
nodes.text: Don’t joke. She disappeared. She was scared before she vanished.

options.text: Scared of who?
When did you last see her?
Back up. Tell me what you actually know.

nodes.speaker: lucy
nodes.text: She didn’t give me names. Just warnings. Told me not to trust the police.

options.text: That narrows it down to everyone with a badge and a pulse.
Why didn’t she tell you more?

nodes.speaker: lucy
nodes.text: Not long before midnight. Long enough to know she wasn’t acting normal.

options.text: Define not normal.
So she knew trouble was coming.

nodes.speaker: lucy
nodes.text: I know she was trying to stay ahead of something. I know she didn’t trust the police. And I know waiting won’t help her.

options.text: Fine. Then give me something real.

nodes.speaker: lucy
nodes.text: And you look like a man who should ask better questions.

options.text: Try me.
You’re protecting somebody.

nodes.speaker: lucy
nodes.text: Fine. I know she was trying to stay ahead of someone. I don’t know if she managed.

options.text: Then start at the beginning.

nodes.speaker: lucy
nodes.text: Maybe I’m protecting what’s left.

options.text: That’s not an answer.
No. But it’s honest enough.

nodes.speaker: lucy
nodes.text: More honest than this city deserves.

options.text: Then help me anyway.

nodes.speaker: lucy
nodes.text: I left the Bar address in the pocket of your jacket. Blondie’s photo should still be on the computer. The Bar is where she was last seen.

options.text: The Bar. Great. A building full of witnesses with selective memory.
I’ll check both.

nodes.speaker: lucy
nodes.text: That still makes it one of the more honest places in this city.

options.text: Comforting.

nodes.speaker: lucy
nodes.text: I do what I can.

nodes.speaker: lucy
nodes.text: Do it fast. Check the jacket, check the computer, and move. If Blondie’s still alive, time is already working for the wrong side.

nodes.speaker: lucy
nodes.text: I tried. They were either drunk, dead, or useless. Then I remembered you.

options.text: You really know how to motivate a man.

nodes.speaker: lucy
nodes.text: And yet, here you are.

nodes.speaker: lucy
nodes.text: Nothing clean. Nothing easy. Just the feeling that she knew something bad was already in motion.

options.text: That feeling usually charges by the hour.
Then I’ll start with the photo and the email.

nodes.speaker: lucy
nodes.text: Then you’d better be worth it tonight.

nodes.speaker: lucy
nodes.text: Good. Your head still works. Use it.

nodes.speaker: lucy
nodes.text: Because saying too much out loud makes things real. And she was still pretending she had time.

nodes.speaker: lucy
nodes.text: Like someone trying to keep her hands steady while her whole future was shaking.

nodes.speaker: lucy
nodes.text: No. I think it was already here.

conditionalFollowups.speaker: lucy
conditionalFollowups.text: Yeah. That’s the one. She hated that photo. Said it made her look too alive for this city.

conditionalFollowups.speaker: lucy
conditionalFollowups.text: That’s the address. Then stop staring at the paper and move. The Bar won’t get more honest while you’re standing here.
